info.title: ouroboros-engine
info.summary: Internal backend for Ouroboros — executes the work ouroboros-rest brokers.
info.description:
The **Python backend** of [Ouroboros](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros): the
service that executes the work `ouroboros-rest` brokers.

It is **internal only**. Every request arrives from `ouroboros-rest`, inside the
cluster, carrying a shared secret on the `X-Ouro-Internal-Key` header; a browser
never reaches it. That is a deployment claim, so the service enforces it itself
rather than trusting it — **every path but `/healthz` requires the key**, the
comparison is constant time, and a request without one is refused before routing.

A rejection is therefore a bare `401 {"detail":"Unauthorized"}` whether the path
exists or not: status codes are how a surface gets mapped from outside, and an
unauthenticated caller cannot tell `/v0/status` from `/v0/anything-else`. Read the
`401` documented on each operation below as the answer to *anything* unauthenticated,
including paths this document does not list.

`/v0` is the versioned internal prefix. It is unstable by definition — it changes
with the two services that share it, which deploy together — and a stable `/v1` is a
later promise, not this one.

servers.description:
`uv run dev`, which binds the loopback interface only. In a deployment the engine
has no public origin at all: it is addressed by its service name from inside the
cluster, and the port comes from `PORT`.

tags.description: Identity and liveness — what answers before any contract does.

tags.name: v0
tags.description:
The versioned internal contract. `/v0/status` claims the path; the request and
error shapes the rest of it follows are
[#52](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/52).

get.description:
Report that the process is up and serving HTTP.

Deliberately shallow: it opens no connection, reads no configuration and calls
nothing downstream, so it cannot fail for a reason that restarting the container
will not fix. *Readiness* — whether the dependencies a request needs are
reachable — is the REST layer's probe, which asks `/v0/status` with the key.

Report which service and which build is answering. Carries no state, reads no
configuration, and says nothing about health — liveness is `/healthz`.

200.description: The service and its installed version.

get.description:
Answer the two questions that come up when the engine is suspected: *which
version of it is this*, and *is this the same process as a minute ago*.

`ouroboros-rest`'s readiness probe is the intended caller. A `401` here means the
two sides hold different secrets, and REST reports that to a client as a `502` —
never a `401`, because the internal boundary is not something a browser gets to
probe.

200.description: The running build and how long it has been running.

InternalKey.name: X-Ouro-Internal-Key
InternalKey.description:
The shared secret both sides of the internal boundary hold: `ouroboros-engine`
reads it from `OURO_ENGINE_SHARED_SECRET`, `ouroboros-rest` sends it. There is no
other credential and no other scheme — no bearer token, no user identity. This
is a service-to-service header, and it is generated per environment.

Unauthorized.description:
The `X-Ouro-Internal-Key` header was missing or wrong. The body is constant: it
names no path, echoes no header and offers no hint about what the key should look
like. What an operator needs is in the engine's log instead, which stays inside
the cluster.

status.description:
Always `ok`. A probe reads the status code; this is for the human who runs
the same request by hand.

service.description: Distribution name of this service, constant across deployments.
Distribution name of this service, constant across deployments.

version.description:
Installed version, read from package metadata — the same string `GET /`
reports, so there is one source for "which build is this".

uptime_seconds.description:
Seconds since this process built its application, rounded to milliseconds.
Small and shrinking across calls means something is restarting the container.

Error.title: Error
Error.description:
The shape every error in this service is reported in. `detail` is FastAPI's own
key, and matching it keeps one shape for a client to parse.

detail.description: A short, constant description of what was refused.
